_readme: Violations of the spider contract (tests/spider_contract.py) that
already existed when the contract was introduced.
tests/test_spider_contract.py xfails everything listed here and
hard-fails anything that is not, so the existing suite stays green
while a new spider is held to the full contract from its first commit.
This file is meant to shrink. Fixing a listed violation makes
test_baseline_has_no_stale_entries fail until its entry is removed, so
the ratchet only tightens. Nothing here is approved behaviour: it is a
C01 may not be listed here. A spider whose fixture parses to nothing
skips every check that needs meetings, so recording C01 would report a
silent pass for the entire contract.
Read HONEST_LIMITS at the bottom of tests/spider_contract.py before
reading a green run as an all-clear. Run

_what_is_listed_and_why.C09: DetCityMixin._parse_location returns {'name': '', 'address': ''} when its .location-info selectors miss, so a meeting can carry a wholly blank location. Only surfaces on the one fixture where the block is absent; the other six spiders on that mixin pass.
_what_is_listed_and_why.C12: The largest group. An empty response body yields no meetings, raises nothing and logs nothing, which is indistinguishable from a page that genuinely had no meetings. This is the shape of the Wayne County failure that went unnoticed for months.
_what_is_listed_and_why.C13: Same as C12 for a half-truncated body. Note limit 4 in HONEST_LIMITS: halving list-shaped input often yields valid rows, so this check passes for some spiders by succeeding rather than by reporting.
_what_is_listed_and_why.C14: Same as C12 for a body with every digit stripped. Note limit 5 in HONEST_LIMITS: stripping digits also corrupts markup, so this exercises broken HTML as much as unparseable dates.
_what_is_listed_and_why.C16: except/pass or except/continue with no logging, which is how one unparseable row becomes one silently missing meeting.
_what_is_listed_and_why.C20: The spider's own parse() raises on its committed fixture, so the engine graded an internal helper instead. These nine are the clearest evidence for limit 1 in HONEST_LIMITS: the checks below them are not covering the path Scrapy calls.

_checks.C01: The fixture parses into at least one meeting
_checks.C02: Meeting ids are prefixed with the spider's own name
_checks.C03: Meeting ids are unique within one run
_checks.C04: Title, start and source are present on every meeting
_checks.C05: End times are absent or after the start
_checks.C06: Datetimes are consistently naive or consistently aware
_checks.C07: Classification is one the framework recognises
_checks.C08: Status is one the framework recognises
_checks.C09: Location is a mapping with name and address
_checks.C10: Links are a list of mappings with a usable href
_checks.C11: Text fields carry no leftover markup
_checks.C12: An empty page is reported, not passed over in silence
_checks.C13: A truncated page is reported, not passed over in silence
_checks.C14: Unparseable dates are reported, not passed over in silence
_checks.C15: Degraded input never yields a malformed meeting
_checks.C20: The spider's own entry point runs without raising on its fixture
_checks.C16: Exceptions are not swallowed without a trace
_checks.C17: The spider does not impersonate a browser
_checks.C18: The spider carries no hardcoded session cookie
_checks.C19: Ids and statuses come from the framework helpers
